bullets: Game 1 of a six-game single-deck session (video 10.3s-225.9s) in which Ryley pushes for world #1 with what he calls "my new piggies deck". The in-game clock OCR failed for the entire video, so every timestamp is a video second and clock times are unknown.

Piloted as defend-then-punish, not as a build-up deck: Cannon at [8, 9]/[10, 11]/[12, 14] with Skeletons, Electro Spirit, Baby Dragon and Mighty Miner on top of the push, then Royal Hogs at the bridge the moment the opponent commits (t=52.1 on a Skeleton-Army-out-of-cycle read, t=112.1 as the Giant lands, t=205.2 as an elixir sink).

Lightning is the deck's plan for a tower, not a defensive tool: first one on the evolved Witch (t=93.1, "the Evo can be super, super annoying if we don't take that off the board"), then two more cycled into the left lane he had already chipped with the hogs (t=143.1, t=169.2) — "I'm going to lightning that musketeer here because I need to get two lightning spells" (t=141-143). Lane choice is explicitly driven by the spell: "I want to Evo piggies here on the right side because I can just lightning cycle the left" (t=136-140).

Mighty Miner does triple duty — chip on offence (enemy left tower 4858 → 2963 at t=38-40), anti-support on defence (placed on the Witch, never on the Bowler, t=158-161), and the closer, with Explosive Escape called out twice at t=206 and t=211 before it takes the enemy right tower at t=216-223.

Ryley's own claims for the list: "I almost never actually lose with this deck" and it is a modified version of an older Tesla variant (t=25-31); "this piggies deck may literally just be the best deck in Clash Royale right now... if you play it extremely well, then you always have a chance" (t=67-75); "it kind of destroys all of the beatdown decks as well minus Lava. You do actually have a chance to beat Lava Hound, but it absolutely destroys like Giant, Golem, you know, Giant Skeleton" (t=77-90).

Cost of the win: the Graveyard chip is never answered — his right tower ends at 787 and his king tower at 1650, which he treats as acceptable ("minimizing damage, but not also like defending poorly", t=196-200). Result read as a win from the commentary at t=216-223 plus the enemy king tower HP becoming readable at t=224; no result banner was OCR'd.

new_deck.rationale: A 3.25-elixir list whose Skeletons / Electro Spirit / The Log / Cannon shell cycles Royal Hogs back faster than the opponent can re-answer them, while Mighty Miner, Baby Dragon and Lightning make it defence-first enough for Control as a genuine secondary.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Every card except Lightning is a defensive answer first: Cannon pulls the tank, Skeletons and Electro Spirit body-block and reset, Baby Dragon covers air and swarms, and Mighty Miner melts whatever the Cannon has pulled — so the Royal Hogs go in only when the opponent has just spent, and never as a committed push. The Log is held almost exclusively for Skeleton Army, the standard hogs counter, which is why Ryley counts elixir out loud before throwing it (t=122-129). Lightning is not a defensive spell here but the deck's finisher: it removes the one card the deck genuinely fears (an evolved Witch) and is then cycled twice into a lane the hogs have already chipped. Ryley's own framing is that the shell beats ground beatdown outright — "it absolutely destroys like Giant, Golem, you know, Giant Skeleton" — and struggles only against Lava Hound (t=77-90).
